 Is China Petroleum & Chemical (SEHK:386) Undervalued As Third Quarter Earnings Land?
 Sasha Jovanovic Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:14 PM EST 4 min read 600028.SS 0.00% 
 0386 
 Third quarter earnings put China Petroleum & Chemical in focus 
 China Petroleum & Chemical (SEHK:386) moved into the spotlight after releasing third quarter 2026 results, with sales of CNY 757,113 million and net income of CNY 13,600 million catching investors' attention. 
 Recent trading has been mixed, with China Petroleum & Chemical's share price slipping 0.62% over the last day and 1.23% over the week, while still posting a 5.95% 1 month share price return and an 18.69% 1 year total shareholder return as the latest earnings are absorbed by the market. 
 Compare China Petroleum & Chemical's earnings momentum with a curated set of potential peers by scanning the 226 high quality undervalued stocks that combine resilient cash flows with stronger balance sheets. 
 After that earnings jump and a modest pullback in the share price, the real tension for China Petroleum & Chemical is clear. Does fair value sit closer to today's HK$4.81 or nearer to the analysts' range ahead? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 8% Undervalued 
 On the narrative view, China Petroleum & Chemical screens as undervalued, with a fair value of HK$5.21 versus the last close at HK$4.81. This puts the focus firmly on how its earnings mix might evolve. 
 Launch of wider cooperation on CCUS projects and low carbon energy, together with ongoing investment in hydrogen, solar, wind and EV charging and swapping, lays out a pipeline of new businesses that can diversify future revenue and earnings beyond road fuel demand. 
 Greater flexibility in crude sourcing, including increased purchases of Russian ESPO crude when Middle East supply tightens, can help China Petroleum & Chemical keep refineries running efficiently and protect fuel export economics, which is important for sustaining refining margins and earnings.

 Result: Fair Value of HK$5.21 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the narrative around China Petroleum & Chemical can weaken if China's fuel demand drops faster than expected or if new energy projects deliver weaker returns. 
 Find out about the key risks to this China Petroleum & Chemical narrative . 
 Another View on China Petroleum & Chemical's Valuation 
 There is a different message coming from China Petroleum & Chemical's P/E. The shares trade on about 12.2x, higher than the Asian Oil and Gas sector at 10.2x and above a 9x peer average, yet below an estimated fair ratio of 13.3x that the market could move toward. 
 That mix of a premium versus the industry but a discount versus the fair ratio points to both valuation risk and possible opportunity, depending on which reference point investors trust more. See what the numbers say about this price — find out in our valuation breakdown.
